solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Enchanting publication I name shortly

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication

indicators.note: cut short, so the synonym for name loses its final letter

parts.note: to call is to name

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a magazine they plan to name will be delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts the last letter from CALL, leaving CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something magical has a spellbinding charm, just as an enchanting thing does.

clue.text: Dangerous driver, crazy, circling right round

indicators.note: the crazy word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: mad means crazy
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A reckless motorist drives madly around in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: Toad, in The Wind in the Willows, is a notoriously reckless motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kenneth Grahame character is famous for crashing motor cars.

clue.text: Choose computer career and take the risk

parts.note: to go for something is to choose it
IT, information technology, is a computing career

explanation.surface: Someone opts for a job in computing and gambles.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhortation to be bold and attempt something daring.

clue.text: Cold, even with president

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
level means even, flat
and means with, together

explanation.surface: A president is chilly, even when in company.
explanation.walkthrough: Grover Cleveland was a US president, twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland was the 22nd and 24th leader of the United States.

clue.text: Long and thin piece of wood, not soft

indicators.note: not here means without, so the soft letter is dropped

parts.note: a plank is a length of timber
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A long thin piece of timber that isn't soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Lank describes something lean and tall, or limp straight hair.

clue.text: Announce two poor grades at college

parts.note: D and E are low exam marks
Clare is a college of Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A student reports getting two bad marks at university.
explanation.walkthrough: CLARE is a Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something is to state it publicly, to announce it.

clue.text: Did initially request a piece of advice, turning up a large book

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of Did

parts.note: to ask is to request

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: Someone asked advice and came upon a hefty volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses TIP to PIT. 'a large book' looks like one phrase but only 'book' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Marx's work on political economy is a famous treatise, a book.

clue.text: Bum died in prison

indicators.note: the died abbreviation goes inside the prison word

parts.note: a cage is a prison

explanation.surface: A tramp died in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' is a verb here, as in bum a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum something is to scrounge it, getting it free by asking.

clue.text: Admits church has added page in holy book

indicators.note: the church and page letters go inside the holy book

parts.note: Acts is a book of the New Testament
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church confesses to inserting a page into scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to accept or acknowledge it.

clue.text: European learning about evil in tragic setting

indicators.note: the learning word goes around the evil word

parts.note: lore is learning, knowledge
sin is evil, wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A European studies evil in a tragedy's setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the learning word around the evil word. 'tragic setting' points to Hamlet, set in this Danish castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish castle where Shakespeare's Hamlet takes place.

clue.text: Time of payments: edited round number gets stuck up

indicators.note: the payments word goes around the number abbreviation

parts.note: fees are payments
ED is an abbreviation for edited or editor

explanation.surface: A schedule of payments, once revised, gets a stuck-up number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts the number inside the payments, giving FEENOS. 'edited' looks like the anagram signal but is just ED.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for snobbish and haughty, like someone who looks down their nose.

clue.text: They order the troops salad

definitions.meaning: a variety of lettuce, a salad plant

explanation.surface: Officers instruct soldiers to eat greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Commanding officers give troops orders; cos is the Romaine lettuce used in salads.

clue.text: Gave approval for a grand instrument

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
a reed is a wind instrument, or its sounding part

explanation.surface: Someone consented to a grand piano or other instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To have consented or said yes is to have given approval.

clue.text: Fixer of team to pinch back

parts.note: a panel is a team of experts or judges

indicators.note: taken backwards, the pinch synonym reads from right to left

parts.note: to nip is to pinch

explanation.surface: A team's fixer gets them to pinch things in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NIP into PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel pin is a small slender nail used to fasten panels.

clue.text: City plaza lies oddly across major road

indicators.note: the plaza and odd letters stretch across the road on both sides

parts.note: a square is a plaza

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of lies

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A city plaza lies oddly across a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st and 3rd letters of 'lies'; 'across' spans those pieces around the road, MI being the M1 motorway. The Square Mile is the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The City of London, the financial district, is nicknamed after its area.

clue.text: Writer in trainers popping pill

indicators.note: the writer goes inside the shuffled letters of trainers
popping suggests things jumping about, so the letters of trainers are mixed

parts.note: a quill is a pen, something you write with

explanation.surface: An author wearing running shoes takes a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popping' shuffles the shoes into TRANISER; 'in' puts the writer inside. 'popping pill' reads as the definition's verb, but only 'pill' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative drug is often taken as a pill or tablet.

clue.text: Old soldier on island line

parts.note: on and leg both name the same side of the field in cricket
Iona is a Scottish island
RY, railway, is a line

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier lives on an island by a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A legionary was a soldier of an ancient Roman legion.

clue.text: Something delightful more than once in middle-class novels

indicators.note: the phrase for something delightful appears twice

parts.note: a gas is something great fun

explanation.surface: Something enjoyable keeps turning up in suburban fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a cast-iron cooker, a symbol of the English country kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aga sagas are light novels of English rural middle-class domestic life.

clue.text: Unseen helper's paper and coin no longer used

parts.note: the Guardian is a British newspaper
the angel was an old English gold coin

explanation.surface: Someone helping in secret owns a newspaper and an obsolete coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is a UK daily newspaper; the angel was a medieval English coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective spirit that watches over a person without being seen.

clue.text: Coming first in race, bumping into a fellow competitor

indicators.note: the first letter of race pushes into the rest

parts.note: a rival competes with you

indicators.note: first in points to the initial letter of race

explanation.surface: A rower wins the race after bumping a rival boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Bumping races are a feature of Oxford and Cambridge college rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is a coming, the act of reaching a place.

clue.text: Having told a story, have to rest

parts.note: telling a story, a fib, is to have lied
to own is to have

explanation.surface: After telling a tale, someone has to take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline in order to recover energy is to rest.

clue.text: My collection of items stays

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!
a set is a collection

explanation.surface: Someone's collected things remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays' looks like a verb but is a noun for a stiffened bodice.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays is an old word for a corset, stiffened with whalebone.

clue.text: Club entertainer ultimately impresses tourist

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of impresses

parts.note: a tripper is a day tourist

explanation.surface: A nightclub performer finally wins over a holidaymaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease artist performs in nightclubs, so is a club entertainer.

clue.text: Part of stomach revolting at bread

parts.note: the pit of the stomach

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so at reads upwards

explanation.surface: Someone feels sick in the stomach at the sight of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' turns AT into TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread.

clue.text: Give up game after opponent captures rook

indicators.note: the game word comes after the rest
the enemy word takes the rook letter inside it, as a chess piece is taken

parts.note: a foe is an opponent
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
go is an Asian board game

explanation.surface: A chess player resigns after an opponent takes a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captures' puts the rook inside the enemy, as in chess; 'after' places the game at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To forego (or forgo) something is to do without it, to relinquish it.

clue.text: Letters associated with pencil broken by Queen Rosemary, perhaps

indicators.note: the queen letters split the pencil letters

parts.note: HB marks a pencil's hardness and blackness
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A pencil inscription is interrupted by the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosemary' looks like a name but is a plant; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic plant used in cooking, an example of the category.

clue.text: Father seen in good sort of light

parts.note: UV, ultraviolet, is a type of light

explanation.surface: A father is viewed favourably.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for governor, a slang form of address for one's dad or boss.

clue.text: After very short time, pastor abandoned defunct browser

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the time word

parts.note: in a trice means in an instant

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters of pastor are jumbled

explanation.surface: A vicar quickly gives up an obsolete web browser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' turns PASTOR into RATOPS. 'Browser' is not a web program but a grazing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This extinct dinosaur browsed on plants, so it was a feeding browser that no longer exists.

clue.text: Recycling: say I'm sorry about Victor's going west

indicators.note: in an across answer, going west means read from right to left

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

indicators.note: the regret word goes around the Victor letter

parts.note: alas expresses regret
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A recycling apology about someone named Victor heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts V inside ALAS (AVLAS); 'going west' reverses EGAVLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is saving discarded material so it can be used again.

clue.text: Sticker finally put on first compartment

indicators.note: the final pick is put on the end of the rest

parts.note: a bay is a compartment, as in a bomb bay
one is the first number

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of put

explanation.surface: A label is finally stuck on the first compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayonet is a blade for stabbing, so humorously it is something that sticks people.
